If we're talking military grade, MOLLE packs come to mind. The assault ones are the best, but any of them will go above and beyond your expectations.

ILBE would be in the middle, I've got a Marpat myself. They're basic and get the job done, but they're not all that comfortable, and have durablity issues. I busted the internal seams on mine, but other than that it performs well.

Stay far away from anything ALICE. If you pack the bag even slightly lopsided, you will end up losing skin on your shoulders

Protip: In addittion to padding, pay attention to the width of the straps. The wider the strap, the more surface area for the weight to be displaced, thus making it easier to carry.

Forgot to mention, lapolicegear.com always has sales going on, you could try there if all else fails.
MOLLE is the coolest thing ever invented!

Like @Gerplunckamo said, assault packs are some of the best for their cost, but they are a bit small IMO.

Things to look for are double stitching on the straps and seams, this greatly increases the life of the pack, especially if you are going inna woods with it. Also make a list of the things you are planning on putting in the pack to make sure you get the right size. Nothing sucks more than getting a new pack and realizing you didn't plan to suit your needs.
If you want a good hiking pack, buy a hiking pack, don't waste your time with military crap.
